title: The quiet triumph of second-hand
text: Second-hand shopping has {{1}} its dusty image and become one of retail's growth stories. Phone apps have {{2}} millions of private wardrobes into a vast, permanently open market, and for younger shoppers, wearing vintage is a {{3}} rather than a compromise: thrift is now a look, not a confession. The economics have followed. Sought-after trainers and jackets can {{4}} their brand-new equivalents, and charity shops report queues for donations that once went unnoticed. One {{5}} is planetary: every reused garment is one not manufactured, and fashion is among the world's most polluting industries. Luxury brands, initially alarmed by the flood of fakes, now {{6}} their own authentication services and official resale programmes, having concluded that a second life for a handbag is better managed by them than by anyone else. Regulators are joining in: France now {{7}} clothing to carry labels disclosing its environmental credentials, and several countries are weighing taxes on freshly made garments. In hindsight, the old stigma never made much {{8}}: clothes were handed down for most of history, and the disposable wardrobe is the historical oddity, not the mended one.

gaps.explanation: 'has shed its dusty image' — cast it off; keep and wear hold on to it, and shun is for avoiding, not losing.
'turned millions of private wardrobes into a market' — converted them; the physical verbs do not transform.
'wearing vintage is a statement rather than a compromise' — a deliberate message; punishment, burden and chore contradict the pride described.
'sought-after trainers can outprice their brand-new equivalents' — cost more than; undercut means cost less, and outrun and outvote are not about price.
'one reason is planetary' — an argument in favour; the benefit described is not a season, an obstacle or a casualty.
'luxury brands now offer their own authentication services' — provide; overturn, forbid and boycott reverse the embrace described.
'France now requires clothing to carry labels' — makes it compulsory; request and invite leave it optional, and let would permit rather than mandate.
'the old stigma never made much sense' — was never logical; progress and headway are made by efforts, and 'waves' would need the plural.
